subject: physics_2
question_text: What is the difference between α-particle and helium atom?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: an α-particle is a helium nucleus — 2 protons and 2 neutrons, charge +2e, no electrons; a helium atom is that same nucleus with 2 electrons around it, so the charges cancel and the atom is neutral.

recall_prompt: Say what an α-particle is made of and what its charge is, then say how a helium atom differs.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The α-particle
lines: An α-particle is the nucleus of a helium atom.
It has 2 protons and 2 neutrons and no
It is emitted in radioactive decay.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Say helium NUCLEUS and give the charge +2e.
steps.why: The α-particle is not a small helium atom — it is the bare nucleus. Naming the two protons fixes the charge at +2e.
common_mistakes: Writing the charge as +e. Two protons give +2e.
Saying the α-particle has electrons. It has none.

recall.must_convey: That an α-particle is a helium nucleus with charge +2e and no electrons.
accept: two protons and two neutrons, no electrons

steps.memory_tip: Strip both electrons off helium and what is left is the α-particle.

steps.label: The helium atom
lines: A helium atom is the same nucleus with 2
electrons around it. The +2e of the nucleus and
the −2e of the electrons cancel, so the atom is
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The atom has its 2 electrons, so it carries no net charge.
steps.why: The whole difference is the two electrons: with them the atom is neutral, without them the same nucleus is a charged α-particle.
common_mistakes: Saying the helium atom has a different nucleus. The nucleus is the same.
Leaving out the reason. The mark is for the cancelling charges.

recall.must_convey: That a helium atom is that nucleus plus 2 electrons, so it is neutral.

steps.memory_tip: Same nucleus, two extra electrons: +2e becomes zero.

insider_note: Both halves are needed — the charge +2e on the α-particle, and the reason the helium atom is neutral.
